page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.8xlarge is a KVM-based virtual machine instance belonging to the ecs.u1 server family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

The underlying x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX and AVX512F), Fast Multiply-Add (FMA), and AES cryptography instructions. These hardware features accelerate vector calculations and cryptographic operations. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache, facilitating efficient data access for multi-threaded workloads.

Performance benchmarks place this instance consistently in the average tier for most operations. It achieves a PassMark CPU score of 34,140.29 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12,692.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 154.63 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 69.38 GB/sec for large block write operations. Notably, the instance demonstrates strong performance in text generation for small LLM models (135M parameters), reaching 304.01 tokens/sec, while medium model (7B parameters) text generation operates at an average speed of 18.54 tokens/sec.

Given its high compute-to-memory ratio, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for CPU-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff. It is suitable for workloads such as multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving, lightweight LLM inference, and general compute-intensive batch processing.
